title: Add M7 regional refinement: level 10 sphere-clipped subset preserving global drainage
description:
## M7 — Regional Refinement (level 10 spherical mesh)

Per .design/realistic-planet-generator.md REQ-16 + AC-16, design.md §5 Stage 6, and plan analysis gap B7. Builds on M0-M6 (main HEAD `48a3786`).

The user explicitly chose spherical (not planar) regional refinement at design-doc time per Q7 resolution.

### In scope

1. **Region selection UI (`src/components/RegionSelector.tsx`)**:
   - User selects a region on the globe by either: painting a polygon, picking lat/lon center + radius, or clicking + dragging a bounding box.
   - Selected region highlights on globe.
   - "Refine region" button triggers worker call.

2. **Sphere-clipped mesh generation (`src/sim/mesh/clipping.ts`)** — builds on M0's clipMeshToRegion:
   - Subdivide the global icosahedron to **level 10** (~10.5M cells, ~8 km/cell) **only within the selected region**.
   - Stays on the sphere — no flat projection (REQ-16 per Q7 resolution).
   - Output: a `MeshData` (per the M0 mesh-type abstraction) representing the clipped subset.
   - WebGPU device must request `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` near hardware max (~2 GiB on RTX 3090) — already done in M0.

3. **Initial state sampling (`src/sim/refinement/sample.ts`)**:
   - For each cell in the level-10 clipped mesh, sample initial state from the global level-8 simulation: elevation, plate ID, crust type, crust age, biome, temperature, precipitation, etc.
   - Use barycentric interpolation across the global cell's neighborhood for smooth interpolation.

4. **Constraint-respecting noise (`src/sim/refinement/noise.ts`)**:
   - Add high-frequency detail to the high-res mesh via fractal noise (Perlin/Simplex).
   - The noise must preserve global drainage structure — rivers existing at level 8 must persist at level 10 and connect to the same outlets (REQ-16).
   - Implementation: noise amplitude tapered toward zero along global river channels and flow direction lines.

5. **Local fluvial erosion (`src/sim/refinement/erosion-local.ts`)**:
   - Re-run M2 erosion + M3 hydrology kernels at level 10 for a small number of steps (~20-50).
   - Same kernels run unchanged thanks to the M0 mesh-type abstraction.
   - Macro structure unchanged (verified by topological comparison).
   - High-frequency tributaries appear only as additions.

6. **Worker integration (`src/sim/worker.ts`)**:
   - Expose `refineRegion(bounds: RegionBounds): Promise<RegionalData>` per design.md §7.4.
   - Returns the level-10 clipped mesh + state buffers.
   - Handles GPU memory: at level 10, buffers can be up to ~1.5 GiB; chunk if needed.

7. **Regional view component (`src/components/RegionalView.tsx`)**:
   - 2D top-down rendering of the regional clipped subset.
   - All M5 layer toggles work (elevation, biome, rivers, etc.).
   - Hex overlay option for VTT-style use (no actual VTT export per design doc — just the visual hex grid).

8. **Tests (`src/sim/refinement/refinement.test.ts`)**:
   - Region selection produces a clipped mesh of expected cell count.
   - Sampling: each cell in the clipped mesh has well-defined initial state.
   - Drainage preservation: a global mesh with N rivers discharging at N ocean cells, when refined, produces N rivers discharging at the SAME ocean cells (per AC-16).
   - High-frequency tributaries appear (cell count of detected rivers in clipped > N + threshold).
   - Macro structure topological comparison: pre-refine and post-refine outlet positions match within tolerance.

### Out of scope (do not start)
- M8/M10 civilization layer — but DO design civilization data structures so they can attach to refined regions later.
- VTT exports (deferred per design doc).

### Acceptance criteria for M7 (from AC-16)
- [ ] Regional refinement uses the same mesh-type abstraction as global; erosion/hydrology/climate kernels run unchanged on the level-10 sphere-clipped subset.
- [ ] For a planet at level 8 with R rivers discharging at R distinct ocean cells, the regional refinement of any chosen region preserves all enclosed rivers and routes them to the same coastline cells.
- [ ] Macro structure unchanged is verified by topological comparison; high-frequency tributaries appear only as additions.
- [ ] M0-M6 test suites still pass after M7 changes (regression).
- [ ] `npm test` + `tsc --noEmit` both pass.
- [ ] No stubs / TODOs.

### Lesson from prior milestones
**Commit each major group separately.** M5/M6 nailed this. M7 has natural commit groups: clipping, sampling, noise, local erosion, worker integration, regional view UI, tests. Aim for 5-7 commits. If batching detected without commits, supervisor will tmux-nudge.

### References
- .design/realistic-planet-generator.md REQ-16 / AC-16
- .design/realistic-planet-generator.plan.json gap B7 (mesh-type abstraction was a CONSCIOUS design choice in M0 specifically to make this milestone clean — pay it off here!)
- design.md §5 Stage 6
- M0 main HEAD 01daaca (mesh-type abstraction + clipMeshToRegion already in place)
- M1-M3 main HEAD 0689470 (tectonics + erosion + hydrology kernels mesh-type-agnostic)
- M6 main HEAD 48a3786 (Layer 2 constraints can attach to refined regions)
